analysts.summary: Consensus is Buy, but the average target ($280) sits ~3% below price (median $296.50). The split is about 15 Buy/Outperform, 12 Hold, 1 Underperform and 1 Sell. Targets were lifted after the S&P add: Mizuho $351, RBC $335, Clear Street $330, Fubon $330 (initiated), UBS $325, Morgan Stanley $310 (Buy), Bernstein $282 (Hold).

bear: Valuation leaves no room for error: ~82x forward P/E and ~16x forward EV/sales, with the price already above the average analyst target.
Securities class action and supply-chain scrutiny over China-sourced scandium; possible tariff or sourcing cost headwinds.
Dilution (+24.7% share count YoY) and steady insider selling; the CEO sold $34M in February.
Customer concentration in hyperscaler AI capex, which the CEO says he can't control. Gas turbines and nuclear compete for the same load. Beta of 3.8 means drawdowns of 30-50% are historically common.
bull: Hyper-growth that is also profitable: +166% revenue, 22.5% non-GAAP operating margin and positive FCF in Q2, with FY26 guidance raised.
Speed-to-power moat: onsite SOFC sidesteps multi-year grid interconnect queues, and all major US hyperscalers are validated customers.
Brookfield's financing grew from $5B to $25B, plus multi-GW sites (Oracle NM 2.45 GW, Aligned PA 2 GW), which gives visibility into 2027-28.
S&P 500 inclusion widens the holder base; low IV percentile vs realized volatility means cheap convexity into Q3 earnings.

competition.summary: Bloom is the scale leader in stationary fuel cells and has become a primary 'bring-your-own-power' supplier for AI data centers. It says every major US hyperscaler has validated it, and it has a ~$20-25B backlog/financing pipeline backed by Brookfield. Its real competition is gas turbines and recip engines (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Caterpillar; Chevron/Microsoft turbine projects) and, longer term, nuclear. Listed fuel-cell rivals are far smaller and loss-making, and Plug Power is explicitly not pursuing data centers. We found no independent market-share figure for onsite data-center power.

summary: Bloom is executing exceptionally: Q2 2026 revenue of $1.065B (+166% YoY), a 22.5% non-GAAP operating margin, positive FCF, and FY26 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B with every major US hyperscaler now a validated customer. But at $289 (~82x forward EPS, ~16x forward EV/sales, S&P 500 entry on Sep 21) the price already sits above the consensus average target ($280) and well above our peer-multiple and earnings-power values. Our triangulated fair value is $190-275 (mid $232, ~20% below price). The business is great, but the stock prices in a lot of perfection, so we stay Neutral: don't chase, and consider adding on pullbacks toward the low-$230s.

valuation.method: Triangulated three ways. (a) Peer multiples: implied NTM EPS ~$3.53 (price / 81.8x forward P/E) at 50-75x, a large growth premium to GEV's 46x, gives $177-265. Implied NTM revenue ~$5.2B at 10-15x EV/sales (2-3x the power-equipment peers) gives $176-264. (b) Earnings power: 2030 revenue $11.6-15B (~30-38% CAGR from the FY26 midpoint), 22-25% operating margin, 21% tax, 30-35x exit P/E, discounted 4 years at 11%, ~300M diluted shares, gives $137-228. (c) Analysts: $97-390, average $280, median $296.5. Blended range $190-275, mid $232.
valuation.note: Revenue growth was not available on the peer statistics pages, so those cells are n/a. BE's premium reflects ~100% growth vs single-digit to mid-teens for the peers. The verdict is sensitive to the multiple: at 90x NTM EPS the stock would be fairly valued.
